item.title: Connecting AI Agents to Live Discrete Element Simulations via the Model Context Protocol
item.description: arXiv:2611.33926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper describes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server through which a general-purpose AI agent operates a discrete element engine, commercial or open-source, while the simulation runs. The agent submits a long simulation to the engine and, while it computes, reads the running model, changes it, or stops it. The human modeler stays at the engine's console and graphical interface throughout, and the agent sees what the modeler does there. The tools are derived from what the agent needs to do at the engine and are held to four principles: correctness, coverage, orthogonality and simplicity. Two documentation tools let the agent search the engine's manual and browse it level by level. Five execution tools let the agent run code in the engine, submit long simulations in the background, check on them, read the running model, and stop them. A bridge inside the engine serves these tools in a commercial DEM engine, PFC, and an open-source one, YADE. In a case study, a general-purpose agent calibrated a drained triaxial model of dense Toyoura sand against laboratory data in both engines, while the modeler worked at the same engine; the agent noticed the modeler's actions at the console and acted on them. The same calibration on YADE was then given to seven language models, three sessions each and without human intervention. Twenty of the twenty-one sessions reached the targets, and nineteen of the parameter sets lie in one small region of the admissible ranges. The server and the bridge are released as two open-source packages, itasca-mcp, which also serves FLAC, 3DEC, MPoint and MassFlow, and yade-mcp.
item.dc:creator: Yusong Han, Ryosuke Uzuoka, Kyohei Ueda

item.title: Bayesian Calibration of Effective Material Parameters in Electric Machine Stators
item.description: arXiv:2611.34071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficiency-driven faster switching by wide-bandgap semiconductor devices increases electromagnetic interference (EMI) in electric vehicles (EVs). Mitigating this EMI becomes more complex as system components grow. Therefore, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is assessed early via system-level simulation of the EV powertrain. A key EMC-critical quantity is the impedance of the electric drive machine, forming a major part of the EMI propagation path. Finite element (FE) simulations are typically used but are computationally expensive and limited by insufficient material property knowledge. We present a surrogate model based Bayesian calibration framework for 3D full-wave FE simulation of an externally excited synchronous motor (EESM) stator. Effective material parameters (EMPs) are calibrated to match broadband differential mode (DM) impedance measurements up to 30 MHz. A multi-output surrogate model replaces the demanding FE simulation, while an orthogonal surrogate model compliant discrepancy term assesses material modeling completeness. Using Hamiltonian Markov Chain Monte Carlo, we construct posterior distributions of the EMPs for three calibration scenarios with different parameter ranges. Two of three scenarios achieve good agreement with measurements. However, accurate calibration requires "datasheet-deviating" EMPs, while "datasheet-aligned" ones yield deficient results, indicating material models do not fully capture the underlying physics. The proposed methodology enables estimating unknown material properties from impedance measurements and evaluates the sufficiency of chosen material models. Although identified EMPs may differ from datasheet values, they reliably estimate frequency-dependent DM impedance. This work focuses on EMPs influencing the stator's DM impedance; complete machine calibration, including rotor and common-mode impedance, is the scope of future research.
item.dc:creator: Patrick D. Gsoels, Christian M. Riener, Markus Flicker, Jose Romero Lopera, Jan P. Henninger, Bibhu Prasad Nayak, Jan Biermann, Bernhard Auinger, Jan C. Hansen

item.title: SCO-Hyper-Meta-Double-GroupNN: A Double-Group SU(2) Hyper-/Meta-Graph Neural Network for Cooperative Spin-Crossover Potential Energy Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.34547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning potential energy surfaces for magnetic materials requires resolving coupled local spin manifolds and geometric frustration. We introduce SCO-Hyper-Meta-Double-GroupNN, a geometry-only architecture combining a pretrained O(3)-equivariant backbone with SU(2) spinor Hamiltonians and cooperative hyper-/meta-graph interactions. Analytic thermal spinor density matrices provide non-polynomial two- and three-body structural invariants, while frustrated-triangle hyperedges and a multi-shell sideway gate couple geometric representations to local spin manifolds. A variationally consistent, doubly-centered zero-gauge free-energy functional couples multiplet occupations and signed spin orientations, yielding conservative autograd forces without spin inputs at inference. On a first-principles Co-Cr-Ni benchmark comprising 346 training and 59 held-out validation supercells across crystalline, amorphous, glassy, and liquid regimes, compact models with 56k-77k parameters outperform a 207k-parameter spin-conditioned magnetic MACE baseline. Energy MAE decreases by 37-44%, reaching 3.82 versus 6.83 meV/atom, and force MAE decreases by 10.8-14.2 meV/Angstrom, reaching 165.8-169.2 versus 180.0 meV/Angstrom. The models preserve Kramers degeneracy to within $6\times10^{-15}$ eV, predict equilibrium local magnetic moments from geometry alone with an absolute-moment MAE of $0.181\,\mu_B$, and support stable molecular dynamics up to 2,200 K. This framework integrates local spinor symmetry and cooperative magnetic interactions into geometry-only interatomic potentials.
item.dc:creator: Rong Fu, Tianhao Su, Shunbo Hu, Musen Li

item.title: Show Your Work: Can Small Open Models Read SEC Filings with Evidence a Machine Can Check?
item.description: arXiv:2611.24990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fluent answer from a language model is not a verified one. We ask whether small open models that run on a single consumer GPU can extract numbers from SEC filings with evidence a machine can check: the page and a verbatim quote containing the number. We introduce Filing-Evidence, a benchmark of 1,000 questions over 90 recent 10-K and 10-Q filings of 45 US companies, with answer keys taken from the filers' inline XBRL tags. We evaluate ten instruct models from ten developers (7-21B parameters) on one RTX 4090 in three setups: plain, check-and-retry, and the model's own reasoning mode. Accuracy with checkable evidence ranges from 17.1% to 82.7% in the plain setup, and the best result is 84.5% (Qwen3.5-9B). An automatic checker rejects many wrong answers, but between 16 and 167 answers per 1,000 give a wrong value for an answerable question and still pass every check. In the plain setup, 57% of these are scale or unit errors and 30% take another period or column of the right line. Reasoning significantly reduces such errors for 4 of 5 models that offer it. Retrying after a failed check raises accuracy by up to 3.9 points but never reduces them. Questions, model outputs, code and protocol are public.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Nandula

item.title: Deep Learning-Based Mesoscopic Emission Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.33179v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Traffic-related emissions are a major contributor to urban air pollution. However, existing emission models face a fundamental trade-off: macroscopic models are computationally efficient but rely on average speeds, leading to systematic errors, while microscopic models achieve high accuracy but are computationally prohibitive for large scale simulations. To bridge this gap, this study introduces Direct Emission Prediction (DEP), a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)-based deep learning model. DEP was trained on over one million synthetic trips generated by coupling real-world GNSS speed profiles with the microscopic emission model MOBSim. By processing sequential link-level inputs, including vehicle characteristics, road attributes, and ambient temperature, DEP predicts CO$_2$ and NOx emissions. We integrated DEP into a MATSim-based workflow and applied it to the Ile-de-France region. DEP matches the accuracy of SPG-M, a hybrid mesoscopic-microscopic reference model, within 0.35% for CO$_2$ and 1.87% for NOx across both hot and cold-start scenarios, while reducing computational runtime to just 2.2%. Furthermore, validation against empirical remote sensing data confirms that DEP accurately reproduces real-world NOx emission levels across Euro 2-6 diesel vehicles, whereas traditional macroscopic tools like COPERT and HBEFA systematically underestimate them. Finally, DEP effectively captures the spatial distribution of cold-start emissions, identifying key hotspots in dense urban areas. This work demonstrates that deep learning-based mesoscopic frameworks can achieve microscopic accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost, enabling scalable, high-resolution urban emission modeling without relying on pre-computed emission factor databases.
item.dc:creator: Abdelkader Dib, Milos Balac, Antonio Sciarretta

item.title: Blind spatially varying PSF estimation for fluorescence microscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.34607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical aberrations degrade fluorescence microscopy images and measuring the underlying point spread function (PSF) often requires dedicated acquisitions or isolated emitters. Here we introduce DeepBlur, a neural network that estimates spatially varying two-dimensional PSFs directly from single images of biological structures. Trained entirely on physical simulations spanning aberrations, illumination and noise, it adapts to diverse imaging conditions without requiring user-supplied optical parameters. Using a deformable mirror, we acquire 1,290 images and assess blind PSF estimates against independent references. DeepBlur estimates agree closely with these references and improve deconvolution of experimentally aberrated images. Local PSF estimation also enables correction of spatially varying defocus and improves random-illumination super-resolution reconstruction in biological tissue. Available through DeepInv, a napari plugin and a web demonstration, DeepBlur can be readily integrated into computational microscopy workflows.
item.dc:creator: Minh Hai Nguyen, Florian Sarron, Paul Escande, Sylvain Cantaloube, Thomas Mangeat, Pierre Weiss

item.title: An Implicit Compact-Kernel Material Point Method for Computational Solid Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2604.18917v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The numerical performance of the material point method (MPM) is strongly governed by the particle-grid kernel, which controls the trade-off among smoothness, locality, numerical diffusion, contact accuracy, and computational cost. Although wide-support smooth kernels can effectively suppress cell-crossing instability, they often introduce increased numerical diffusion, artificial contact gaps, and higher transfer cost. In contrast, the suitability of compact-kernel designs for implicit computational solid mechanics remains unclear. In this work, we develop an implicit formulation of the Compact-Kernel Material Point Method (CK-MPM) building on the framework of Liu et al. [2025], and assess its performance through benchmark problems in linear and nonlinear solid mechanics. Numerical assessment comprises cantilever bending, Hertzian contact, narrow-clearance free fall, and colliding hyperelastic rings, supplemented by a transfer-only diffusion test and spatial and temporal refinement studies. Implicit CK-MPM mitigates the cell-crossing stress noise and numerical energy loss observed in linear MPM, while retaining bending and energy responses comparable to those of quadratic B-spline MPM. Meanwhile, its more localized transfers improve contact-pressure accuracy and reduce the artificial contact gaps and early-contact artifacts associated with the wider-support quadratic kernel. These results demonstrate that the developed implicit formulation retains CK-MPM's favorable balance between smoothness and transfer locality in static and dynamic solid-mechanics analysis.
item.dc:creator: Qirui Fu, Yupeng Jiang, Minchen Li

item.title: Mechanical Modeling of Braided Neurovascular Flow Diverters using a Beam-to-Beam and Beam-to-Surface Contact Formulation
item.description: arXiv:2607.29446v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Braided neurovascular flow diverters are widely used for the endovascular treatment of intracranial aneurysms. Their mechanical response and deployed configuration are governed by the interaction of many slender, interwoven wires, which makes the numerical simulation of the complete device a challenging problem. This work presents a detailed mechanical model of complete braided flow diverters that integrates geometrically exact beam mechanics and contact mechanics into one consistent implicit finite element formulation. Every wire is modeled as a geometrically exact Simo-Reissner beam, which consistently describes large rotations and curved reference configurations. The interactions between the wires are captured by a beam-to-beam contact formulation with a history-dependent gap function that prevents unintended wire crossings. The interaction with surrounding tubular structures, such as microcatheters or crimping devices, is captured by a beam-to-surface contact formulation. A parametric description of interwoven braided geometries enables systematic control of design parameters such as wire count, braiding angle, device length, and interweaving pattern. The model is assessed by means of three test cases from the literature. A tensile test investigates the length-diameter relation and the axial force response, and a radial compression test addresses the pressure-diameter behavior. A stepwise compression example evaluates geometry-sensitive quantities, including local wire distance, helix angle, porosity, and metal coverage ratio. The results show that the model captures both the characteristic mechanical response and clinically relevant geometric quantities of braided flow diverters.
item.dc:creator: Martin Frank, Ivo Steinbrecher, Matthias Mayr, Alexander Popp

item.title: OpenTherm: A Unified and Progressive Benchmark for 2.5D/3D-IC Thermal Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2608.23977v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate and efficient chip thermal prediction is essential for advanced packaging design. In recent years, deep learning-based thermal predictors have made significant progress, achieving high prediction accuracy while substantially reducing computational costs. However, differences in datasets, simulators, and evaluation protocols hinder direct comparison of existing methods and systematic assessment of their generalization across design variations and cross-package transfer scenarios. We introduce OpenTherm, an open benchmark combining 32,000 established 3D-IC samples with 50,000 new 2.5D chiplet samples generated with the open-source HotSpot simulator. It provides fixed data splits, a common input representation, and shared evaluation tools. Five deployment-aligned Generalization Scopes cover fixed-design workload prediction, within-family layout, material, and cooling exploration, and cross-package out-of-distribution (OOD) transfer with few-shot adaptation. Under a shared protocol, eight model configurations show gradual error growth within known package families. The best MAE increases by 13.7x from the broadest within-family scope to zero-shot cross-package transfer. Larger models do not consistently generalize better, and ten labeled fields per unseen package reduce MAE by 76-93%. Project site: https://github.com/Day333/OpenTherm.
item.dc:creator: David Hang, Wenkai Yang, Kuiye Ding, Haiyang Xin, Jacky Wei

item.title: ADformer: A Multi-Granularity Spatial-Temporal Transformer for EEG-Based Alzheimer Detection
item.description: arXiv:2409.00032v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Electroencephalography has emerged as a cost-effective, efficient tool to help neurologists detect Alzheimer's Disease. However, most existing approaches rely heavily on manual feature engineering or data transformation. While these techniques may help with small-scale datasets, they often cause information loss and distortion when applied to large-scale data, ultimately limiting model performance. Moreover, the limited subject scale and demographic diversity of datasets used in prior studies hinder comprehensive evaluation of model robustness and generalizability, thus restricting their applicability in real-world clinical settings. To address these challenges, we propose ADformer, a novel multi-granularity spatial-temporal transformer that captures both temporal and spatial features from raw EEG signals, enabling effective end-to-end representation learning. Our model introduces multi-granularity embedding strategies across both spatial and temporal dimensions, leveraging a two-stage intra-inter-granularity self-attention mechanism to learn local patterns within each granularity and global dependencies across granularities. We evaluate ADformer on 4 large-scale datasets totaling 1,713 subjects, one of the largest corpora for EEG-based AD detection to date, under a cross-validated, subject-independent setting. Experimental results demonstrate that ADformer consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving subject-level F1 scores of 87.11%, 89.83%, 67.99%, and 84.42% on the 4 datasets, respectively, in distinguishing Alzheimer's Disease patients from healthy control subjects.
item.dc:creator: Yihe Wang, Nadia Mammone, Darina Petrovsky, Alexandros T. Tzallas, Francesco C. Morabito, Xiang Zhang

item.title: Automated classification of modal displacements
item.description: arXiv:2611.31472v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The bending, torsional, or coupled character of a mode shape helps determine the dynamic behaviour of aerospace and civil structures. In vibration testing, it is assigned by inspecting mode shape plots, and depends on the analyst. This work proposes four indices to describe the motion of a mode from a few sensor vectors: a bending score, a torsion score, a twist share and an in-plane ratio. They are assessed on the first eight finite element modes of a tapered plate with a swept trailing edge. They are applied to identified XB-2 wing modes and to the published modes of the Sheraton Universal Hotel, a reinforced concrete (RC) building. On the plate, the twist share separates bending, coupled and torsion modes. The XB-2 modes include one bending and three coupled modes (one dominated by in-plane bending and two by out-of-plane bending). The coupled mode dominated by in-plane bending (15.25 Hz, in-plane ratio 1.33) was not investigated in earlier campaigns on the wing. On the RC building, all five modes are bending (twist share below 0.0005). The twist share and the in-plane ratio indicate the type of each mode. Hence, modes are classified without visually inspecting the mode shapes. Code and processed data are openly released.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Dessena, Marco Civera, Saray Undiano Ech\'aniz, Oscar Bonilla-Manrique
